subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be closed by accepting the shared session-init serialization/self-heal direction, or should maintainers require explicit retry/coalescing parity for WebChat, heartbeat, and other inbound lanes before closure?
rationale: The code now has partial shared serialization and Slack retry precedent, but the issue discussion distinguishes transient message drops from the permanent wedge fixed by the open PR, so the remaining owner boundary is a maintainer product and architecture choice.

options.title: Require Shared Retry/Coalesce Proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a shared fix or coordinated surface fixes prove that transient reply-session-init conflicts preserve inbound events on WebChat and heartbeat.

options.title: Land Self-Heal Then Re-Test
options.body: Treat the open self-heal PR as the first fix path, but do not close this issue until transient distinct-message WebChat/heartbeat proof is captured afterward.

options.title: Accept Current Main
options.body: Close only if maintainers determine the current writer-lane serialization is sufficient and can supply focused proof for the reported transient lanes.

recommendation.title: Require Shared Retry/Coalesce Proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a shared fix or coordinated surface fixes prove that transient reply-session-init conflicts preserve inbound events on WebChat and heartbeat.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest recent history on the session accessor and guarded initialization boundary where the shared-versus-surface recovery choice sits.
